messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thanks. I want a fair financial share, and I won’t subsidize A’s discounted purchase. I haven’t agreed to it. I’m open to hearing her reasons, but there’s no rush—we can work out the options together.

I’d like to buy the house with my husband, and a family discount is part of what would make that workable for us. I can’t give a clear financial picture or set a fair price yet; nothing is settled. I want B and C to have a real say, and I know I need C’s agreement.

I could use some money from the estate to start a dance studio. I haven’t settled what I’d like to happen with the house; I know A hopes to buy it, and that C hasn’t agreed. I’d want the amount and everyone’s shares to be worked out fairly.
Yes, an independent valuation is a fair starting point. I’m not agreeing to a price or discount yet; we should make sure everyone’s share is clear before deciding.
An independent valuation seems sensible, but I can’t agree in advance to paying market value or to an open sale. I’d want to see the valuation and discuss options with B and C first.
That seems a sensible place to start. I’d also like us to work out what money could come to me for the studio once the valuation and everyone’s shares are clear.
Yes, compare both options after the valuation and A’s finances are clear. Before agreeing to a sale, I’d want everyone’s shares and any sale costs clarified.
I’m willing to compare both routes after the valuation. I can’t share a clear financial picture right now, and I don’t know whether buying near the valuation would be affordable for us.
Yes, that plan sounds fair. I haven’t worked out a reliable studio budget yet, so I’d rather not guess at an amount; once the valuation and shares are clear, I can work out what I’d need.
